comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C61, C62, C66 regarding amino acid substitutions in recognition sequences. Both evaluations find the data in Figure 2 convincing and support the conclusion that specific amino acids can replace proline. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on claims C77-C81 regarding TEV protease and proline protection strategies. Both evaluations accept these methodological approaches as valid solutions with supporting experimental data. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on claims C115-C122 regarding cyclization/polymerization data. Both accept the concentration-dependent assembly distributions and mechanistic interpretations. OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate as SUPPORTED, treating this as a valid application of the method.

Strong agreement on abstract claims C7-C13 summarizing overall method capabilities. Both evaluations affirm the high efficiency, versatility, and broad applicability. Peer reviewers describe 'compelling well-controlled data' while OpenEval validates claims against experimental results. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Substantial overlap on protein fusion data (C69-C76). OpenEval R3 focuses on SDS-PAGE systematic data and LC-MS validation (C69-C76, C82), while peer R2 covers broader production claims (C67-C76). Both strongly support the high conversion efficiency findings. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on antibody conjugation claims C93-C96, C100-C104. Both evaluations accept the high labeling efficiency (97%) demonstrated by convergent SDS-PAGE and LC-MS data. Both note this as a key demonstration of method utility. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on BcPAP characterization. OpenEval R2 covers production yields (C67-C68), LC-MS specificity (C84), and inhibitor sensitivity (C86, C88). Peer R4 focuses on serine protease classification (C85, C86, C88). Both accept the characterization data. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on conjugation homogeneity. OpenEval R6 addresses LC-MS distribution data (C105-C109) showing 95% homogeneity for larger assemblies. Peer R5 includes these claims (C106-C109) within broader antibody conjugation evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Significant disagreement on linker length limitations (C151-C154, C156). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting concerns haven't been observed and framing as balanced evaluation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly raising long linker as 'biggest drawback' that may interfere with protein folding and limit applicability to native protein studies.

Partial overlap on sequence requirements and method comparison (C143-C150). OpenEval R13 rates characterization as SUPPORTED with balanced assessment. Peer R8 focuses on limitations (C151-C154) and rates as UNCERTAIN due to linker concerns. Different emphasis on strengths vs. limitations.

Partial agreement on comparative advantages over Sortase (C2-C4). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting broad claims lack rigorous head-to-head comparison. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting comparative advantages and noting absence of side reactions. Peer evaluation is more accepting of comparative claims.

Partial overlap on summary claims C126-C127. OpenEval R10 validates these accurately reflect demonstrated capabilities. Peer R7 strongly supports overall method with similar claims. Both rate as SUPPORTED, though peer evaluation is more enthusiastic about broader impact.

Minimal overlap on cyclization conclusions (C123-C124). OpenEval R9 notes need for substrate-specific optimization. Peer R6 accepts cyclization as valid application without noting optimization requirements. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on BcPAP production yields (C67-C68). OpenEval R2 includes these within broader characterization. Peer R2 explicitly notes identification of BcPAP as key finding. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on LC-MS specificity data (C84). OpenEval R2 includes this within BcPAP characterization showing 99.8% proline removal. Peer R3 accepts LC-MS confirmation as part of thorough characterization. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on LC-MS validation (C82). OpenEval R3 emphasizes orthogonal validation showing 99.6% product formation. Peer R3 accepts mass spec confirmation without detailed discussion. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on stability data (C98). OpenEval R7 notes limited detail but accepts claim with figure support. Peer R5 includes this within broader antibody conjugation evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
OpenEval R11 addresses replacement mechanism and purification strategy (C128-C131) with supporting data in Figure 6. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R12 addresses re-conjugation applications (C132-C137), rating as UNCERTAIN because claims are largely speculative without experimental demonstration. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R15 discusses competing Sortase A method (C139-C142) with appropriate citations, rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific comparison.

OpenEval R18 addresses sweeping comparative claim C157 about method being 'unmatched', rating as UNCERTAIN due to lack of systematic head-to-head comparisons. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

Peer R9 addresses comparative advantages over Sortase (C2-C4, C48) including absence of side reactions, rating as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R16 partially overlaps but focuses on broader comparative claims and rates as UNCERTAIN.
